name: Marty
def: Grey tower robot with googly eyes that roams supermarket aisles looking for spills and hazards and checking shelves for stock and price errors.
body: Marty stands about 6 feet 5 inches tall on a wheeled base, with cameras and lidar that watch the floor for liquid and debris and the shelves for gaps and mispriced items. It navigates a stored store map during trading hours, alerting staff over the store system when it finds a hazard. Its cartoon eyes and name were a deliberate attempt to make an in store robot feel approachable to shoppers. Nearly 500 units were rolled out across Giant, Martin's and Stop and Shop stores in 2019.
facts: Nearly 500 units rolled out across Giant, Martin's and Stop and Shop stores in 2019
Stop and Shop upgraded Marty units at more than 300 locations in 2023
Reported accuracy of about 95 percent on out of stock detection by one customer
specs: Wheeled base with a tall sensor mast
Cameras and lidar with floor facing hazard detection
Map based navigation among shoppers with automatic alerts to staff
